fields.label: Is Default Module
fields.description: This module is the linked entity's default home — where it opens when nothing else decides — even when another app defines it. A sidebar that already lists the entity still holds you, so this settles cold entry rather than overriding where you are. Flag what you mean to own: a claim is declarative, so set it on the entities your app is about rather than only where you expect the default to disagree with you. Only an app-shipped sidebar may claim.

fields.label: Route
fields.description: Path inside the page, e.g. "payroll" opens /desk/<page>/payroll. No leading slash, query or fragment.

fields.label: Customization
fields.description: Only meaningful on a `Custom Sidebar`, where a row is either a reference to a base item or an item the site or the user added.

fields.label: Hidden
fields.description: Hide this item. Explicit rather than implied by the row's presence, which is what lets a user's `hidden: 0` un-hide something the site hid.

fields.label: Added
fields.description: 0 means this row references a base item: non-empty fields override it, empty fields mean no opinion. 1 means a full item the layer added, rendered as it stands.

fields.label: Key
fields.description: Only meaningful on a `Custom Sidebar` row referring to a base item that has no link -- a Section Break or a spacer -- which is the one kind of row with nothing else to name it by. A base row stores none: an unlinked one is identified by a hash of its type and label, and a linked one by its own link columns, which is what lets a rename repair the base row and the customization naming it together.
